title: SIREN Reauthorization Act
official_summary:
Supporting and Improving Rural EMS Needs Reauthorization Act or the SIREN Reauthorization Act

This act reauthorizes through FY2028 and otherwise modifies a grant program for improving emergency medical services (EMS) in rural areas. The modifications include requiring the use of grant funds to train EMS personnel on caring for individuals with mental health and substance use disorders in emergency situations and permitting the use of grant funds to acquire overdose reversal drugs and devices.

summary.headline: Law extends a federal grant program for rural emergency medical services through 2028 and changes how the money can be used.
summary.what_it_does: This law renews a federal grant program that helps improve emergency medical services (EMS) in rural areas, keeping it funded through fiscal year 2028. Grant money must now be used in part to train EMS workers on caring for people with mental health and substance use disorders during emergencies. Grant money can also be used to buy overdose reversal drugs and devices.

who_it_affects.how: They can keep applying for federal grants through 2028 and may use the money to buy overdose reversal drugs and devices.
Grant-funded agencies must train them on handling emergencies involving people with mental health or substance use disorders.
Their local emergency medical services may receive continued federal grant support.

who_it_affects.group: People with mental health or substance use disorders in rural areas
who_it_affects.how: EMS crews responding to their emergencies may have more specific training and access to overdose reversal tools.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 26, 2024; the grant program is reauthorized through fiscal year 2028.
